content: Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride, when co-administered with certain medications, can lead to significant pharmacological interactions. These interactions may increase the risk of adverse effects such as seizures, arrhythmias, renal impairment, or other toxicities. Below are detailed descriptions of these interactions: 1. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and amphotericin B phospholipid complex: Co-administration increases the toxicity of amphotericin B due to fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. This can heighten the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 2. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and anagrelide: This combination increases toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, which can predispose patients to serious cardiac arrhythmias. Preand post-colonoscopy ECGs should be considered in high-risk patients. 3. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and aripiprazole: The effects of aripiprazole are enhanced through an unknown mechanism. Close monitoring for central nervous system (CNS) depression is recommended, especially at higher doses. 4. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and arsenic trioxide: Co-administration increases toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is advised for patients at risk of cardiac arrhythmias. 5. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and asenapine: This combination increases both the toxicity (via QTc prolongation) and the effects of asenapine through an unknown mechanism. CNS depression should be closely monitored. 6. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and aspirin: Co-administration increases aspirin toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, raising the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution is advised. 7. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and atracurium: Magnesium potentiates the effects of neuromuscular blocking agents like atracurium. Close monitoring is necessary to avoid excessive neuromuscular blockade. 8. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and azilsartan: Co-administration increases azilsartan toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. This can lead to seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution is advised. 9. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and baloxavir marboxil: Magnesium decreases the levels of baloxavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies or dose adjustments are recommended. 10. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and benazepril: Co-administration increases benazepril toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and betamethasone: This combination increases betamethasone toxicity, likely due to fluid and electrolyte disturbances. Monitoring is essential. 12. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and bictégravir: Magnesium reduces bictégravir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Patients should take bictégravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing medications. 13. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and bisacodyl: Co-administration increases the risk of mucosal ulceration or ischemic colitis. Avoidance or alternative therapies are recommended. 14. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and bumetanide: This combination increases bumetanide toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and buprenorphine: Co-administration increases buprenorphine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended for high-risk patients. 16. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and calcium acetate: Co-administration increases calcium acetate toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte disturbances. Monitoring is necessary. 17. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and calcium carbonate: This combination increases calcium carbonate toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and calcium chloride: Co-administration increases calcium chloride toxicity. Monitoring is essential. 19. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and calcium citrate: This combination increases calcium citrate toxicity. Caution is advised. 20. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and calcium gluconate: Co-administration increases calcium gluconate toxicity. Monitoring is necessary. 21. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and calcium/vitamin D: This combination increases toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Monitoring is essential. 22. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and candesartan: Co-administration increases candesartan toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and captopril: This combination increases captopril toxicity. Monitoring is necessary. 24. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and carbonyl iron: Magnesium reduces carbonyl iron levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Iron products should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing medications. 25. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and carboplatin: Co-administration increases carboplatin toxicity. Monitoring is essential. 26. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and cariprazine: This combination enhances cariprazine effects through an unknown mechanism. CNS depression should be closely monitored. 27. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and celecoxib: Co-administration increases celecoxib toxicity. Monitoring is necessary. 28. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and chlorothiazide: This combination increases chlorothiazide toxicity. Monitoring is essential. 29. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and chlorpromazine: Co-administration increases chlorpromazine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Magnesium also reduces chlorpromazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Chlorpromazine should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing medications. 30. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and chlorthalidone: This combination increases chlorthalidone toxicity. Monitoring is necessary. 31. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and choline magnesium trisalicylate: Co-administration increases toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Monitoring is essential. 32. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ciprofloxacin: Magnesium reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Fluoroquinolones should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing medications. 33. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and cisatracurium: Magnesium potentiates the effects of neuromuscular blocking agents like cisatracurium. Monitoring is necessary. 34. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and cisplatin: Co-administration increases cisplatin toxicity. Monitoring is essential. 35. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and citalopram: This combination enhances citalopram effects through an unknown mechanism. Monitoring for seizures is recommended when used with drugs that lower the seizure threshold. 36. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and clofazimine: Co-administration increases clofazimine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is advised for high-risk patients. 37. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and clomipramine: This combination enhances clomipramine effects through an unknown mechanism. Monitoring for seizures is recommended. 38. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and clozapine: Co-administration enhances clozapine effects through an unknown mechanism. CNS depression should be closely monitored. 39. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and corticotropin: This combination increases corticotropin toxicity. Monitoring is necessary. 40. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and cortisone: Co-administration increases cortisone toxicity. Monitoring is essential. 41. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and cyclophosphamide: This combination increases cyclophosphamide toxicity. Monitoring is necessary. 42. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and deferiprone: Magnesium reduces deferiprone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Deferiprone should be administered at least 2 hours before or after magnesium-containing medications. 43. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and deflazacort: Co-administration increases deflazacort toxicity. Monitoring is essential. 44. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and delafloxacin: Magnesium reduces delafloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Fluoroquinolones should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing medications. 45. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and demeclocycline: Magnesium reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Tetracyclines should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing medications. 46. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and desipramine: This combination enhances desipramine effects through an unknown mechanism. Monitoring for seizures is recommended. 47. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and dexamethasone: Co-administration increases dexamethasone toxicity. Monitoring is necessary. 48. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and diclofenac: This combination increases diclofenac toxicity. Monitoring is essential.
